clue.text: Tool, one used to catch mice?

definitions.meaning: a person used by another as a dupe or instrument, as in the fable of the monkey and the cat
literally the foot of a feline, the thing a mouser grabs with

explanation.surface: Someone asks what tool would do for catching mice.
explanation.definitionFit: A dupe manipulated into doing someone's dirty work is called this, after the fable where a monkey uses a cat's foot to pull chestnuts from a fire.

clue.text: All out there, Greek doctors?

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island, so Greek can clue it
MO is medical officer, a doctor; MOS is the plural

explanation.surface: A question about whether all the medics out there are Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is everything that exists out there, the whole ordered creation.

clue.text: See 24
Sweet confection's ultimate in licence for vitality?

indicators.note: for here links vitality to what follows, the vitality word standing in front

parts.note: pep means energy or vitality

indicators.note: in places the last letter inside the word for licence

parts.note: a permit is a licence

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so the final letter of confection's is taken

explanation.surface: A sweet treat is pictured as permission to feel lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate' picks the final letter of confection's, and 'in' slots it before the last letter of the licence word; 'for' lets the vitality word come first.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint-flavoured sweet is a type of confectionery, so it is an example of a sweet.

clue.text: Pipe takes a period of time to fill cart

indicators.note: to fill means the cart word is stuffed with the other letters

parts.note: a wain is an old farm cart or wagon
a term is a period of time, such as a school term

explanation.surface: A pipe being loaded into a cart takes a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fill' splits the old cart word after its first letter; 'takes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The main underground pipe carrying the public supply of drinking liquid is a type of pipe.

clue.text: Wise getting pet in, as barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so these letters go crazy into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sensible takes in a dog, which happens to be barking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' rearranges PETINAS; the dog suggested by 'pet' and 'barking' is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a formal synonym for wise or sagacious.

clue.text: Ordering rosé? Me, I'm left to translate!

definitions.text: Ordering rosé? Me, I'm left to translate!

indicators.note: translate here means change into another form, so the letters are converted into a new order

parts.note: the accent is dropped, leaving the letters R O S E
the apostrophe is dropped, leaving I and M

explanation.surface: A diner ordering pink wine is left to make sense of a foreign wine list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to translate' rearranges ROSEMEIML; the whole clue is also the scene of a wine waiter left to explain an order.
explanation.definitionFit: The wine waiter in a restaurant is the person a diner leans on when ordering and interpreting a wine list.

clue.text: Capital half lost — that's a nuisance

indicators.note: the city was formed from two halves, Buda and the other one, so one half goes missing

parts.note: Budapest is the capital of Hungary

explanation.surface: Losing half a capital city is called a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Budapest was formed in 1873 by uniting Buda and Pest, so 'half lost' drops BUDA.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritating person or thing is a nuisance, a common synonym.

clue.text: English friend carrying American agency's waste away

indicators.note: carrying means the friend word holds the agency inside it

parts.note: mate is British slang for a friend
the CIA is the American intelligence agency; the 's reads as is

explanation.surface: An English friend helping a US agency wastes away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' splits the friend word in the middle to hold the agency; mate is everyday British for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to become abnormally thin, that is to waste away through illness or hunger.

clue.text: References can be seen by everyone wearing the Asian garment

indicators.note: wearing means the everyone letter is dressed in, so sits inside, the garment

parts.note: a sari is a garment worn in South Asia
a U certificate marks a British film as suitable for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A modest garment is described as fit for everyone to see.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing; 'wearing' tucks it inside the garment, just before its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Books of synonyms are reference works, so the plural word is an example of references.

clue.text: See 19
Accommodating agreement, rival losing to Guardian tortoise?

parts.note: The Times is a rival newspaper to the Guardian
in Aesop's fable the hare lost the race to the tortoise, here cast as the Guardian

explanation.surface: A rival newspaper is cast as the hare beaten by the Guardian's tortoise.
explanation.walkthrough: The rival paper is both TIMES and the HARE losing a fable race to the Guardian as tortoise.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal for shared ownership of a holiday property is an agreement about accommodation, punningly 'accommodating'.

clue.text: Disappointing conclusion in West End show, even in colour

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the show's title

parts.note: Oliver! is a long-running London musical, the West End being London's theatre district

indicators.note: conclusion means the final letter of Disappointing is used

parts.note: e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: A West End show ends disappointingly, even with its colourful staging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' slips the last letter of Disappointing before the show's final R; the poetic e'en stands for even.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull yellowish shade like unripe drupes from the Mediterranean tree is a named colour.

clue.text: Casual greeting, more lofty on the telephone?

indicators.note: a word heard over the phone is taken by its sound only

parts.note: higher means more lofty

explanation.surface: Someone says a casual hello in a posh phone voice.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal hello, a friendly greeting used between people who know each other.

clue.text: World of entertainment, Mickey Mouse deadly sin inspiring revulsion in the end

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the jumbled letters take in the extra one
Mickey Mouse means shoddy or amateurish, so these letters are botched into a new order
in the end means the final letter of revulsion

explanation.surface: Mickey Mouse is accused of a deadly sin that ends in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mickey Mouse' rearranges DEADLYSIN and 'inspiring' takes in N, the last letter of revulsion. Mickey looks like part of the scene, which fits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian theme park is a realm devoted to amusement, a world of entertainment.

clue.text: A politician catching balls initially is clumsy with both hands

indicators.note: catching means the politician word holds the other letters

parts.note: a minister is a government politician

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of balls

explanation.surface: A politician drops a catch, proving clumsy with both hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' opens the politician word after its first letter; 'initially' picks the opening letter of balls.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare word means equally awkward with either hand, the opposite of ambidextrous.

clue.text: Collapse, seeing rascal thus eaten up by wild animal

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a rascal

indicators.note: eaten means swallowed by the animal, so placed inside it

parts.note: a lion is a wild animal

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for thus runs bottom to top

parts.note: so means thus

explanation.surface: A rascal is seen being devoured by a wild beast.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down entry 'up' turns the word for thus to run upward, and 'eaten' places the result between the beast's third and fourth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An inward collapse, as of a building or vessel crushed by external pressure, is a kind of collapse.

clue.text: Hit songs stirring up racism

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters of the words up racism into a new order

explanation.surface: Popular songs are accused of stoking racism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' rearranges UPRACISM; 'Hit' looks like chart success but puns on a rap as a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip-hop songs are a genre of music, and a rap is also a hit or knock, which gives the pun.

clue.text: Fairies on yellow dish

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian myth, so two of them give the doubled word
yellow and chicken both mean cowardly

explanation.surface: Fairies are perched on a yellow plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the fairies above the yellow word in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Poultry cooked in a hot African chilli sauce is a popular restaurant dish.

clue.text: Wonderful Guardian popular — hopeful about it

indicators.note: about means the hopeful word goes round the other letters

parts.note: aspiring means hopeful of achieving something
the Guardian refers to itself in editorials as we
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that the Guardian is popular and hopes for more.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian speaks of itself as 'we' in editorials; 'about' opens the hopeful word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that fills one with awe and wonder is wonderful in the original sense.

clue.text: Provocative evening performance somewhere in Hollywood

definitions.meaning: a striptease, a provocative act, held at dusk
a famous stretch of ... Boulevard in West Hollywood

explanation.surface: A risqué night-time show is staged somewhere in Hollywood.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous stretch of boulevard in Los Angeles is a place in Hollywood, and literally a striptease at dusk.

clue.text: Beginning to erupt, chief of clan producing gas

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of erupt

parts.note: a thane was a Scottish clan chief or lord

explanation.surface: A volcano starts to erupt and a clan chief produces gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A colourless flammable hydrocarbon found in natural gas, so an example of a gas.

clue.text: See 4
Something unwanted on one's back, case for a tuxedo?

parts.note: a monkey on one's back is a burden or addiction one cannot shake off
a suit is a lawsuit, a case in court

explanation.surface: A burden on someone's back is wondered about as a reason for formal dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for formal evening dress, especially a dinner jacket outfit, so a tuxedo.

clue.text: Diamond, did you say? Prepare to propose!

indicators.note: did you say asks whether the word was heard correctly, signalling a word that sounds like it

parts.note: Neil Diamond is the American singer-songwriter

explanation.surface: A suitor fusses about a diamond ring before proposing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamond' looks like the engagement ring but is the singer Neil Diamond.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down on one knee is the traditional preparation for asking for someone's hand in marriage.

clue.text: Old criminal, man spotted then shot, routine having backfired

parts.note: spotted dick is a British pudding, so a spotted man is a Dick

indicators.note: having backfired means the words for shot and routine go backwards

parts.note: a nip is a shot or small measure of spirits
a rut is a dull routine

explanation.surface: A man is seen and then shot after his routine went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted dick is a British steamed suet pudding with currants. 'having backfired' turns NIPRUT around.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth-century English highwayman, hanged in 1739, is a famous criminal of old.

clue.text: Tireless working to keep one clean

indicators.note: to keep means the jumbled letters hold the extra one inside
working means the letters of Tireless are worked into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone works tirelessly to keep things clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges TIRELESS and 'to keep' holds I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sterilise is to make free of germs, a thorough way to clean.

clue.text: A ship's heading into the drink — here?

definitions.text: A ship's heading into the drink — here?

indicators.note: into means that first letter goes inside the drink word

parts.note: tea is a drink

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of ship's

explanation.surface: A ship heads out into the drink and someone asks where it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts S (the heading of ship's) inside TEA. 'The drink' is also slang for the sea, which makes the whole clue the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel out on the ocean is on the water, which is also the idiom for being bewildered.

clue.text: See 17
Lager-swilling female somewhat regretted alcoholism, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection means the letters are read as in a mirror, back to front
somewhat means only part of the words regretted alcoholism is used

explanation.surface: A boozy woman somewhat regrets her drinking on reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes ETTEDAL from regretted alcoholism and 'on reflection' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a young woman who drinks heavily and behaves boisterously, like the lads.
